To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bandgap is not renormalized, that the carrier cooling is slow and that the radiative lifetime is not temperature dependent.
the carrier capture and relaxation processes in 1D structures are very slow and that the 1D carrier cooling is appreciably reduced compared to 2D structures.

(i) 1D band renormalization effects are absent in our high quality structures, (ii) carrier cooling in 2D is much faster than in 1D and (iii) the temperature dependence of the recombination lifetime is not in line with theoretical predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of fundamental processes such as carrier capture, cooling and recombination in semiconductor quantum wires, which have been studied in the past mainly in quantum wells, but which can be expected to be of particular importance in quantum wire structures, due to their one-dimensional character.
the fundamental understanding of carrier dynamics in semiconductor quantum wires and their application as active elements of novel optoelectronic devices.
the investigation of fundamental physical processes in semiconductor nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1D structures show a reduced carrier cooling and a reduced bandgap renormalizing effect.
the recombination kinetics in one-dimensional systems is not different in any essential respect from that of two- or three-dimensional structures.

the 1D quantum wires investigated are of excellent optical and structural quality, with no 1D band renormalization and with a carrier temperature that is higher than that in 2D structures of comparable quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombination kinetics in semiconductor 1D structures is not fundamentally different from the recombination kinetics of 2D structures.
the 1D carrier dynamics is not as much affected as expected by the reduced dimensionality.
we found a very good agreement between theory and experiment in the case of 2D systems, whereas the theoretical predictions fail to explain the observed behaviour in one-dimensional structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 1D carrier system in a high quality semiconductor quantum wire is very different from the 2D case.
the 1D carrier dynamics are governed by the same physical processes as in the corresponding 2D case, but the 1D dynamics are slower.
1D structures are very promising for the realization of high quality, high efficiency, and high speed light sources.
